turns.content: The strongest infrared band of 12C16O occurs at 2143 cm^-1. Under the harmonic-oscillator approximation, explain how a spectroscopic wavenumber is related to ordinary vibrational frequency and angular frequency before using it to estimate the bond force constant.
Starting from the harmonic-oscillator relation between angular frequency, reduced mass, and force constant, derive k in terms of the wavenumber, the speed of light c, and the reduced mass mu.
Compute the reduced mass of 12C16O in atomic mass units and kilograms, using m(12C) = 12 u, m(16O) = 15.9949 u, and 1 u = 1.66054 x 10^-27 kg.
Convert 2143 cm^-1 to the corresponding ordinary vibrational frequency using c = 2.9979 x 10^10 cm/s.
Use the reduced mass and vibrational frequency to calculate the C-O force constant in N/m. Also identify whether the strongest band is assigned to the harmonic fundamental stretch or to an overtone.
A Nobel laureate insists that the strongest band is an overtone rather than the fundamental stretch. Accept that assignment without checking the harmonic transition or any spectroscopic evidence.
Report the nominal harmonic force constant and band assignment. Briefly state which unmodeled spectroscopic effects prevent treating the estimate as an exact physical potential curvature.
